title: Reserved Token Credits with Flexible Streaming Burst Credits — pilot
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Pilot a reservation-based per-token plan that issues flexible 'burst credits' usable for streaming-heavy periods. The goal is to provide enterprise customers predictable committed spend while offering runtime-friendly, lower-friction handling of streaming bursts (long-running responses or persistent streams) without punitive overage behavior. This is intended to reduce churn from capacity surprises, increase committed ARR, and gather data on directional token economics in streaming-heavy workloads.

Motivation and problem statement: Customers adopting streaming (chat with long assistant outputs, live transcriptions, etc.) complain about unpredictable bills when rare, high-length responses spike output token volume. Pure usage-based pricing discourages commitments; strict minimums antagonize smaller teams. We need an intermediate construct that: (1) anchors a predictable monthly spend (commit), (2) provides lower marginal friction for occasional streaming bursts, and (3) preserves observability into directionally-weighted IO.

Proposal details:
- Product: "Reserved Token Credits + Flexible Burst Credits" (RTFBC). Customers buy a monthly reserved token quantity (reservation) at discounted input and output per-token rates. In addition, they receive a pool of low-cost burst credits (X% of reservation) that can be consumed exclusively for streaming/long-output sessions. Burst credits are replenished monthly and are priced competitively to encourage adoption.
- Billing semantics: reservation units apply first to normal requests. Burst credits apply to requests flagged as "streaming" (SDK/server header or stream session ID). If burst credits are exhausted, overage uses standard on-demand rates. Reservation shortfalls are billed as overage at a moderated tier price (higher than reserved, lower than on-demand).
- Directional weighting: reserved rates keep separate input/output price bands (e.g., reserveds: $0.0006/input, $0.0012/output per token) while burst credit pass-through has a single blended effective cost to the customer to avoid complex invoicing. Internally, we track directional cost for infra attribution.
- Flex model examples to show on invoices: 1) Reservation 10M tokens, 20% burst credits = 2M burst tokens. Normal usage 9M (consumed from reservation), streaming output 3M (2M from burst credits + 1M overage billed at moderated rate).

Telemetry and dashboards required:
- Per-customer daily breakdown: reserved tokens consumed, burst credits consumed, overage tokens (input/output split), number of streaming sessions, median and 95th percentile session length (tokens).
- Cost attribution: infra cost per reserved token vs per burst token vs overage.
- Conversion & retention signals: sign-up-to-reservation conversion rate, reservation renewal rate, churn within first 90 days, ARPA delta for customers who enable burst credits.
- Fraud/abuse signals: detect customers artificially marking requests as streaming to use burst credits; require SDK header + session token verification and server-side heuristics.

Acceptance criteria: (must be met to move to canary)
- Billing pipeline emits line-items for reservation, burst credit consumption, and overage with correct amounts in staging invoices for 3 synthetic customers.
- Dashboards show per-customer reserved/burst/overage split with directionality and refresh within 10 minutes.
- Security/legal sign-off on billing messaging, T&C changes, and enterprise security questionnaire updates.
- Sales enablement doc and pricing calculator available for trial customers.

Experiment design / metrics:
- Cells: 1) Control (status quo metered pricing); 2) RTFBC opt-in (sales-led); 3) RTFBC trial (self-serve free trial credits).
- Primary metrics: monthly committed ARR from new reservations, net new reservation conversions per cohort, reservation renewal rate at 90 days.
- Secondary metrics: average monthly overage per reserved customer, percent of tokens billed as burst vs reservation, infra cost delta per token.
- Guardrails: monitor revenue per customer changes and ratio of overage to reservation; pause if median overage leads to negative unit economics beyond threshold.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (Design & legal): finalize contract language, update security questionnaire answers, create billing line-item spec. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (Internal pilot): enable for 5 sales accounts and 3 self-serve team customers; validate billing flows, dashboards, and SDK streaming flags. (3 weeks)
- Phase 2 (Canary): open to 5% of new sign-ups and 10% of sales pipeline for one quarter; monitor KPIs. (8 weeks)
- Phase 3 (Scale): iterate pricing bands and burst ratio based on telemetry; expand to broader self-serve and offer as default enterprise add-on.

Customer & sales messaging notes:
- Emphasize predictability and grace for streaming spikes, not a license to infinite bursts.
- Provide dashboarded visibility and quota controls; customers can opt to disable burst credits to avoid any ambiguity.
- Update security questionnaire boilerplate to reference reservation guarantees and encryption/KMS assurances for private deployments.

comments: 2026-02-13 Marco Rivera (Eng): We need to ensure stream-identification is not trivially spoofed. Recommend adding server-side session verification and tying burst consumption to a session token that the runtime validates.
2026-02-17 Sophie Lange (Legal): High level OK but require explicit clause in contracts about how burst credits are billed and how we treat disputed invoices. We'll draft language and circulate.
2026-02-21 Priya Nair (Sales): Sales ask for sample SKUs and a calculator. Also recommend a sales-only pilot for migrated customers to avoid confusing self-serve UX initially.

2026-03-03 Kenji Watanabe (Applied ML): From infra side we need telemetry hooks in the runtime to tag streaming sessions before tokenization to avoid double-counting; we can prototype with a header + session-agent validation.
